name: Route purchase requests from Slack to approval and create POs in NetSuite with Claude

parameters.content:
## Route purchase requests from Slack to approval and create POs in NetSuite with Claude

Finance and operations teams that approve purchases in email threads and lose track of them.

### How it works
Trigger: A purchase-request form (or a Slack slash command) starts the workflow; email requests to procurement@ are parsed the same way.
1. Receive the request
2. Normalise and complete
3. Check budget and policy
4. Route approvals
5. Create the PO
6. Send to the supplier
7. Track receipt
8. Report committed spend
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items; the write-back waits for an approval.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus NetSuite / Dynamics / Xero, Slack.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Set the approval thresholds and the approver map in the Config node; swap NetSuite for Dynamics or Xero.
Guardrail to keep: No PO is created without the approvals the policy matrix requires; the workflow enforces, it does not decide.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/purchase-order-automation/

## 1. Receive the request
What, why, quantity, estimated cost, needed-by date, requester and cost centre — from a form or a Slack message

## 2. Normalise and complete
Maps the free-text item to a category, suggests the preferred supplier from the catalogue, fills the budget line from the cost centre, and asks the requester for anything missing

## 3. Check budget and policy
Remaining budget for the line from the finance system; policy rules (three quotes above a threshold, contracted supplier required for a category, blocked categories)

## 4. Route approvals
Approval chain by amount and category: manager, budget owner, procurement, finance — each in Slack with the request summary; reminders and escalation after the SLA

## 5. Create the PO
Approved request becomes a PO in the ERP (NetSuite, Dynamics, SAP B1, Xero) with the approvals attached

## 6. Send to the supplier
PO emailed from procurement with terms and delivery details; supplier acknowledgement tracked

## 7. Track receipt
Expected delivery dates monitored; the requester confirms receipt (or partial receipt) from a Slack prompt, which closes the PO for invoice matching

## 8. Report committed spend
Live view of requested, approved, ordered and received spend by cost centre and category; approval cycle time by step

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Purchase request form / Slack
- Supplier catalogue and contracts
- Budget system (ERP or FP&A tool)
- ERP purchasing module
- Approval policy matrix (finance-owned sheet)

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Normalise and complete" step of the Purchase Order Automation workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Maps the free-text item to a category, suggests the preferred supplier from the catalogue, fills the budget line from the cost centre, and asks the requester for anything missing.

Rules:
- No PO is created without the approvals the policy matrix requires; the workflow enforces, it does not decide.
- Supplier suggestions come from the approved catalogue; new suppliers go through onboarding first.
- Budget checks use live data; over-budget requests are flagged, not blocked silently.
- Every step is logged with actor and timestamp for audit.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
